functions.name: area
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of surface area of the shell elements.

functions.name: beta
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of shell system beta angle. This is defined as the angle between the element local system x-axis and the material system x-axis. In radians measured counter-clockwise from the element local x-axis.

functions.name: component_id
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the ID of shell component id.

functions.name: density
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the density of shell elements.

functions.name: depth_factor
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the depth factor at which stresses have been recovered. The depth equals Ft/2 where t is the shell element thickness. F values equal to +1.0 or -1.0 correspond to the outer/inner shell surface. The outer surface is defined by the positive z-direction of the local shell element system. F values of 0.0 corresponds to the shell mid-surface. The depth factor can be modified with the \(structure shell recover stress\) command.

functions.name: element_type
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the name of the finite-element type used by the shell elements. The possible types for shell elements are ‘cst’, ‘csth’, ‘dkt’, ‘dkt-cst’, and ‘dkt-csth’.

functions.name: extra
functions.signature: itasca.structure.shellarray.extra(slot: int) -> array float{shell} or float{shell,3}
functions.description: Get the shell extra data in the given slot as an array. Extra variables accessed by array must be of type float or vec.

functions.name: force_nodal
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the generalized nodal force acting on the shell at each node. The translational and rotational components of node 1 are given first.

functions.name: id
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the ID of shell element id.

functions.name: in_group
functions.description: Return shell group membership as a Boolean array.

functions.name: local_system
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the local coordinate system of shell elements.

functions.name: mark
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the mark flag of shell elements.

functions.name: poisson
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the Poisson’s ratio of the elements.

functions.name: pos
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the current position of shell elements.

functions.name: pressure
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the uniform pressure acting on the shell elements. A positive value acts in the z-direction of the element local system.

functions.name: prop_anis
functions.signature: itasca.structure.shellarray.prop_anis() -> (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)
functions.description: Get the anisotropic material properties. Material-stiffness coefficients c’11, c’12, c’13, c’22, c’23, c’33 are returned for both the membrane and bending stiffnesses in that order. If the element does not have anisotropic properties, zeros are returned.

returns.type: (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)

functions.name: prop_ortho
functions.signature: itasca.structure.shellarray.prop_ortho() -> (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)
functions.description: Get the orthotropic material properties. Material-stiffness coefficients c’11, c’12, c’13, c’22, c’23, c’33 are returned for both the membrane and bending stiffnesses in that order. If the element does not have orthotropic properties, zeros are returned.

returns.type: (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)

functions.name: prop_type
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the material property type. Possible return values are ‘isotropic’, ‘orthotripc’, and ‘anisotropic’.

functions.name: resultant
functions.signature: itasca.structure.shellarray.resultant(location: int) -> length 8 tuple of array float{shell}
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of stress resultants last calculated for the element at the index \(location\). A \(location\) value of 0 gives the resultant at the element centroid; \(location\) values 1, 2 and 3 give the resultant at the nodes. The components in the return value are: Mx, My, Mxy, Nx, Ny, Nxy, Qx and Qy. Note that stress resultants must be calculated with the \(structure shell recover\) command. See also the \(resultant_valid\) method.

functions.name: resultant_valid
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of of the stress resultant validity flag. True indicates that the stress resultant values are valid. False indicates that resultants have not been calculated or that there has been a change since they were last calculated that would invalidate the results.

functions.name: set_density
functions.description: Set the density of shell elements.

functions.name: set_extra
functions.signature: itasca.structure.shellarray.set_extra(slot: int, data: array float{shell} or float{shell, 3}) -> None
functions.description: Set the shell extra data in the given slot with an array. Extra variables set by array must be of type float or vec.

functions.name: set_group
functions.signature: itasca.structure.shellarray.set_group(membership: array bool{shell}, group_name: str, slot=1) -> None
functions.description: Set shell group from an array. Where membership True set the corresponding shell to be a member of group group_name in the given slot.

functions.name: set_mark
functions.description: Set the mark flag of shell elements.

functions.name: set_poisson
functions.description: Set the Poisson’s ratio of the elements.

functions.name: set_pressure
functions.description: Set the uniform pressure acting on the shell elements. A positive value acts in the z-direction of the element local system.

functions.name: set_thermal_expansion
functions.description: Set the thermal expansion coefficient of shell elements.

functions.name: set_thickness
functions.description: Set the element thickness.

functions.name: set_young
functions.description: Set the Youngs modulus of the elements.

functions.name: stress
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the stresses at the current depth factor at the index \(location\). A \(location\) value of 0 gives the stress at the element centroid; \(location\) values 1, 2 and 3 give the stress at the nodes. Stresses are expressed in the global system. Note that compressive stresses are negative.

functions.name: stress_prin
functions.description: Get the resolved principal stress at the current depth factor at the index \(location\). A \(location\) value of 0 gives the stress at the element centroid; \(location\) values 1, 2 and 3 give the stress at the nodes. Returns a vector encoded as (minimum, intermediate, maximum). Note that compressive stresses are negative in FLAC3D.

functions.name: stress_valid
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the stress validity flag for the element. True indicates that the stresses last calculated at the current depth factor are valid. Galse indicates that stresses have not been calculated, or that there has been a change that invalidates the last stresses calculated.

functions.name: thermal_expansion
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the thermal expansion coefficient of shell elements.

functions.name: thickness
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the element thickness.

functions.name: type
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the type name of shell elements.

functions.name: volume
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the element volume, or surface area times thickness.

functions.name: young
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the Youngs modulus of the elements. Modifying the value during cycling may be a danger.
